source: NY Senate (A10679-B / S10274); RISMedia; Brick Underground

headline: New York reins in
*private listings*
slides.sub: Gov. Hochul signed the Fair and Transparent Real Estate Listings Act on Nov. 20.

slides.title: Public by *default*
points: Listings must be marketed *in a timely way* on platforms open to the public.
It covers both *home sales and rentals*.
Sellers and landlords can still opt out, but only by signing a *state disclosure form*.
The form warns of fewer buyers, fewer offers and a *possibly lower price*.

slides.label: top fine for agents who *break the rule*
slides.body: Violations can also lead to a suspended or revoked license. Connecticut signed a similar opt-out law in May.

slides.title: Seller choice, *on paper*
slides.body: Private and early-access marketing is not banned, but it now requires a signed, plain-language warning. Walking sellers through the trade-offs in writing is becoming the norm.
